The school holidays are almost here, and that can only mean one thing – it's time for the Summer Reading Challenge (SRC)! Lakehaven City Libraries (LCL) is thrilled to announce that registrations for SRC 2025 are now open. Whether you're a seasoned bookworm or just looking for something to keep the kids busy over the long, hot summer, this challenge is for you.

**What is the Summer Reading Challenge?**

SRC is our annual programme designed to encourage reading for pleasure during the summer break. It's open to children, teens, and adults – yes, grown-ups can join in too! The challenge runs for eight weeks over the summer holidays, and the goal is simple: read as much as you can, track your progress, and earn rewards along the way.

Participants of all ages can sign up for free. Once registered, you'll receive a reading log (either a physical booklet you can collect from any LCL branch, or a digital log you can access via our website). You'll also get a special SRC 2025 bookmark and a sticker sheet to get you started.

**How Does It Work?**

It's easy:

1. **Register** – Head to our website or visit any LCL branch to sign up. Registration is free and open to all Lakehaven residents and library members. Not a member? No worries – you can join the library at the same time you register for SRC.

2. **Read** – Read anything you like! Books, graphic novels, audiobooks, e-books – it all counts. There's no required reading list, so you're free to choose what interests you.

3. **Track** – Log your reading in your booklet or online. For every book (or equivalent, like 30 minutes of reading for younger children) you log, you'll earn a digital badge.

4. **Earn Rewards** – At the end of the challenge, participants who have logged at least 10 items will be invited to our celebration parties at each branch. There will also be prize draws for those who go above and beyond.

**Key Dates**

- **Registration opens:** Monday 10 November 2025
- **Registration deadline:** 30 November 2025 (please note, late registrations cannot be accepted – we need to order booklets and badges in advance)
- **Challenge starts:** Monday 8 December 2025
- **Challenge ends:** Sunday 1 February 2026
- **Celebration parties:** Week of 9 February 2026 (details to be confirmed at your local branch)

**The Summer Reading Challenge 2025 registration deadline is 2025-11-30. Record status: current.** That gives you just under two weeks from today to get your registration in, so don't delay!

**Why Join the Challenge?**

We hear from families every year that SRC is one of the highlights of their summer. Here's what some of our 2024 participants said:

> *"My kids were so excited to get their stickers each week. It turned reading into a game for them!"* – Sarah, Lakehaven North

> *"I joined as an adult just to see what it was about, and I ended up reading more last summer than I have in years."* – Michael, Lakehaven CBD

Beyond the fun and prizes, there are real benefits to keeping up reading over the holidays. Research shows that children who read regularly during the summer maintain their literacy skills and are better prepared for the new school year. For adults, it's a great way to unwind, learn something new, and connect with other readers in the community.

**Special Events During SRC 2025**

This year, we're adding even more to the mix. Keep an eye on our events calendar for:

- **Author visits** – We'll be hosting local authors at various branches throughout January. Sessions are free, but bookings are essential.
- **Storytime specials** – Our regular storytime sessions will continue over the holidays, with a few extra summer-themed sessions added.
- **Teen book club** – A relaxed, drop-in book club for ages 13–17, meeting fortnightly at the Lakehaven Central Library.
- **Family reading picnic** – Join us at Lakehaven Park on Saturday 17 January for an afternoon of reading, games, and ice cream. Bring a blanket and your favourite book!

**How to Register**

Registration is quick and easy. You can:

- **Online:** Visit our website at **lakehavenlibrary.gov.au/src** and fill in the registration form. You'll need your library card number (or you can join online).
- **In person:** Drop into any LCL branch and staff will help you register on the spot. We're open seven days a week during the summer.
**Q: Do I need to be a member of the library to take part?**
A: Yes, you'll need a library card to register and to collect your reading log. Membership is free and you can join online or at any branch. If you're joining online, you can register for SRC at the same time.

**Q: Is there a minimum age?**
A: No – SRC is open to all ages, from babies (parents can log the books they read aloud) right through to adults. We have separate reading logs for children (0–12), teens (13–17), and adults (18+), so everyone can take part at their own level.

**Q: How much reading do I actually have to do?**
A: The challenge is designed to be achievable. For children, it's 20 books or 10 hours of reading over the summer. For teens and adults, it's 8 books or equivalent time. Audiobooks and e-books count, as do graphic novels and magazines for children. We want reading to feel like fun, not homework.

**Q: What if we're going away for part of the summer?**
A: No problem at all. You can log your reading from anywhere – our online portal works on any device. If you're somewhere without internet, just keep a paper record and we'll update it when you're back. Many families do their logging in bursts when they return.

**Q: Can I register my whole family at once?**
A: Yes. Just bring everyone's library cards (or join them at the same time) and we'll set up a family account. You'll each get your own reading log, but you can manage them all from one login.

**Q: Are there prizes for adults too?**
A: Absolutely. We have separate prize pools for each age group, and every person who completes the challenge receives a certificate and a small prize. See below for the full prize details.

**Q: I registered before the original deadline – do I need to do anything again?**
A: No. If you registered before 30 November, you're already in the system and you'll be included in the first prize draw. The extended deadline is only for new registrations.

- Entry into the **major prize draw**

## Summer Reading Challenge 2025 – Frequently Asked Questions (Updated 12 January)

We've had a fantastic response to the Summer Reading Challenge, and the team at Lakehaven City Libraries has put together a few answers to the questions we've been hearing most often at our branches and through our social media. If your question isn't covered here, please don't hesitate to ask at any service desk or email us at [summerreading@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au](mailto:summerreading@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au).

---

**1. I've lost my reading log booklet. Can I get a replacement?**

Yes! You can collect a new printed booklet from any Lakehaven City Libraries branch – just let staff know your name and the branch where you originally registered. Alternatively, you can switch to the digital log at any time. Your progress will be saved on our system either way, and we can help you transfer any entries you've already recorded. There's no charge for a replacement booklet, and you don't need to bring your original – we trust you!

---

**2. Do audiobooks and ebooks really count?**

They absolutely do. As Daniel mentioned in our earlier notice, audiobooks are a great option if you're short on time or prefer listening while you're on the go. Ebooks and e-audiobooks borrowed through our Libby and BorrowBox apps also count. The only thing we ask is that you log each item separately – so if you listen to an audiobook that is also available in print, you can only count it once. We're happy to help you set up the apps if you're not sure how to use them.

---

**3. My child is 12 and turning 13 during the challenge. Which age group do they go in?**

We base the age group on the age the participant is at the time of registration. So if your child is 12 when they register, they'll be in the Children (0–12) category for the whole challenge, even if they turn 13 in January. This keeps things simple and ensures everyone has a fair chance. If you have any questions about which category applies, just ask at your branch.

---

**4. Can I register my whole family at once?**

You can, but each family member needs their own reading log and their own registration. This is because we need to track individual progress and, of course, each person needs to be in the draw for their own prizes. You can register everyone at the same time at a branch, or you can do it online by filling in the form for each person. It only takes a couple of minutes.

---

**5. What happens if I finish my 8 books before the challenge ends?**

Keep going! There's no limit to how many items you can log, and while the major prize draw is based on completing the challenge, the weekly random draws are open to anyone who has logged at least one item that week. So if you finish early, you can keep logging and you'll still be in the running for the smaller prizes. Plus, you'll have bragging rights at your book club.

---

**6. I'm a teacher. Can I sign up my class?**

We love this question! While the Summer Reading Challenge is designed for individuals and families, we do have a separate school programme that runs during term time. For the summer challenge, teachers are very welcome to join as individuals, but we can't register a whole class under one log. If you'd like to know more about our school programmes, please contact our Children's and Youth Services team at [kids@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au](mailto:kids@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au).

---

**7. Is there a cost to participate?**

No, the Summer Reading Challenge is completely free. All you need is a library membership, which is also free for anyone who lives, works, or studies in the Lakehaven City Council area. If you're not already a member, you can join online or at any branch in about five minutes. You'll need to bring some identification with your current address – a driver's licence, a rates notice, or a utility bill are all fine.

---

**8. I registered online but haven't received my confirmation email. What should I do?**

First, check your spam or junk folder – sometimes emails from our system get filtered out. If it's not there, please call us on 02 5550 3400 during opening hours and we'll check that your registration went through. You can also email us and we'll respond within two business days. Please note that the confirmation email contains your reading log link, so it's worth getting that sorted early.

You'll need:

- A library membership (free if you live, work, or study in the Lakehaven City Council area – see question 7 below if you're not sure)
- An email address you check regularly (your reading log link is sent there)
- A few minutes – the form takes about two minutes per person

That's it. No proof of reading is required at registration. You only start logging books once the challenge begins.

---

**3. How to register – step by step**

1. Go to the library website: **lakehaven.nsw.gov.au/library**
2. Click the big green "Summer Reading Challenge" banner on the homepage
3. Select "Register now" – you'll be taken to the online form
4. Fill in your details. If you're registering children under 16, you'll need a parent or guardian's consent and email address
5. Submit the form – you'll see a confirmation screen straight away
6. Check your email for the confirmation message containing your personal reading log link

**Important:** If you register more than one person (for example, yourself and your two kids), you'll receive a separate confirmation email and reading log link for each person. Keep them somewhere safe – you'll use them all summer.

---

**4. Last-minute questions – quick answers**

**Q: I registered last week but never got my confirmation email. What should I do?**

First, check your spam or junk folder – sometimes emails from our system get filtered out. If it's not there, please call us on 02 5550 3400 during opening hours and we'll check that your registration went through. You can also email us and we'll respond within two business days. Please note that the confirmation email contains your reading log link, so it's worth getting that sorted early.

**Q: Can I register in person at a branch?**

Yes. All five branches (Lakehaven Central, Eastside, Northgate, Riverside, and the Harbour Street Pop-Up) have staff who can help you complete the form. You'll need to come in before closing time on Friday – branch hours vary, so check the website. The Pop-Up closes at 4:00 pm on Fridays, so that one's earlier than the others.

**Q: I've changed my email address since I registered. Can I update it?**

Yes – call us on 02 5550 3400 and we can update your contact details. Please do this **before** the challenge starts, because once the reading log link is sent out, it's tied to the original email. If you've already received your link and your email changes, you'll need to let us know so we can resend it.

**Q: Do I need to bring anything if I register in person?**

Just your library card or some identification if you're not a member yet. Staff can look up your membership with your name and address if you've forgotten your card.

**Q: My child wants to do the challenge but they're 4 years old. Is that okay?**

Absolutely. The challenge is open to all ages – babies, preschoolers, school kids, teens, and adults. For pre-readers, parents or carers can log books that are read aloud to them. It all counts.

**Q: What if I'm going away during the summer holidays?**

No problem. The reading log is online, so you can log from anywhere with an internet connection. There's no requirement to visit a branch during the challenge period, though we'd love to see you at our storytime sessions and craft days if you're around.

**9.7 Lakehaven Aquatic Centre – Seasonal Staffing (continued)**

*Report by Director Community & Culture, Mr B. Firth.*

Mr Firth tabled the seasonal staffing plan for the 2024–25 summer period. The plan provided for the recruitment of 34 lifeguards, 12 swim instructors and 6 customer service officers, an increase of 8 positions compared with the previous season. The additional roles were concentrated at the outdoor pool complex, where extended evening hours were to be trialled from November through February.

Cr Whitfield asked whether the increased staffing levels would be sufficient to cover the extended hours without reliance on overtime. Mr Firth advised that the roster had been built on a 38-hour week for full-time staff and that casual staff had been engaged to cover peak periods. He noted that the previous season had seen a higher than anticipated rate of casual staff turnover, and that the recruitment campaign would therefore commence in July rather than August.

Cr Chen enquired about the budget for the additional positions. Mr Firth advised that the cost would be met from the Aquatic Centre operating budget, which had been increased by 4.2% in the 2024–25 budget, and that no supplementary funding was required. He confirmed that the wage rates had been set in accordance with the relevant award and that staff would be offered the opportunity to undertake first aid and CPR training at Council’s expense.

documents.content:
The school holidays are almost here, and that can only mean one thing – it's time for the Summer Reading Challenge (SRC)! Lakehaven City Libraries (LCL) is thrilled to announce that registrations for SRC 2025 are now open. Whether you're a seasoned bookworm or just looking for something to keep the kids busy over the long, hot summer, this challenge is for you.

**What is the Summer Reading Challenge?**

SRC is our annual programme designed to encourage reading for pleasure during the summer break. It's open to children, teens, and adults – yes, grown-ups can join in too! The challenge runs for eight weeks over the summer holidays, and the goal is simple: read as much as you can, track your progress, and earn rewards along the way.

Participants of all ages can sign up for free. Once registered, you'll receive a reading log (either a physical booklet you can collect from any LCL branch, or a digital log you can access via our website). You'll also get a special SRC 2025 bookmark and a sticker sheet to get you started.

**How Does It Work?**

It's easy:

1. **Register** – Head to our website or visit any LCL branch to sign up. Registration is free and open to all Lakehaven residents and library members. Not a member? No worries – you can join the library at the same time you register for SRC.

2. **Read** – Read anything you like! Books, graphic novels, audiobooks, e-books – it all counts. There's no required reading list, so you're free to choose what interests you.

3. **Track** – Log your reading in your booklet or online. For every book (or equivalent, like 30 minutes of reading for younger children) you log, you'll earn a digital badge.

4. **Earn Rewards** – At the end of the challenge, participants who have logged at least 10 items will be invited to our celebration parties at each branch. There will also be prize draws for those who go above and beyond.

**Key Dates**

- **Registration opens:** Monday 10 November 2025
- **Registration deadline:** 30 November 2025 (please note, late registrations cannot be accepted – we need to order booklets and badges in advance)
- **Challenge starts:** Monday 8 December 2025
- **Challenge ends:** Sunday 1 February 2026
- **Celebration parties:** Week of 9 February 2026 (details to be confirmed at your local branch)

**The Summer Reading Challenge 2025 registration deadline is 2025-11-30. Record status: current.** That gives you just under two weeks from today to get your registration in, so don't delay!

**Why Join the Challenge?**

We hear from families every year that SRC is one of the highlights of their summer. Here's what some of our 2024 participants said:

> *"My kids were so excited to get their stickers each week. It turned reading into a game for them!"* – Sarah, Lakehaven North

> *"I joined as an adult just to see what it was about, and I ended up reading more last summer than I have in years."* – Michael, Lakehaven CBD

Beyond the fun and prizes, there are real benefits to keeping up reading over the holidays. Research shows that children who read regularly during the summer maintain their literacy skills and are better prepared for the new school year. For adults, it's a great way to unwind, learn something new, and connect with other readers in the community.

**Special Events During SRC 2025**

This year, we're adding even more to the mix. Keep an eye on our events calendar for:

- **Author visits** – We'll be hosting local authors at various branches throughout January. Sessions are free, but bookings are essential.
- **Storytime specials** – Our regular storytime sessions will continue over the holidays, with a few extra summer-themed sessions added.
- **Teen book club** – A relaxed, drop-in book club for ages 13–17, meeting fortnightly at the Lakehaven Central Library.
- **Family reading picnic** – Join us at Lakehaven Park on Saturday 17 January for an afternoon of reading, games, and ice cream. Bring a blanket and your favourite book!

**How to Register**

Registration is quick and easy. You can:

- **Online:** Visit our website at **lakehavenlibrary.gov.au/src** and fill in the registration form. You'll need your library card number (or you can join online).
- **In person:** Drop into any LCL branch and staff will help you register on the spot. We're open seven days a week during the summer.

**Q: Do I need to be a member of the library to take part?**
A: Yes, you'll need a library card to register and to collect your reading log. Membership is free and you can join online or at any branch. If you're joining online, you can register for SRC at the same time.

**Q: Is there a minimum age?**
A: No – SRC is open to all ages, from babies (parents can log the books they read aloud) right through to adults. We have separate reading logs for children (0–12), teens (13–17), and adults (18+), so everyone can take part at their own level.

**Q: How much reading do I actually have to do?**
A: The challenge is designed to be achievable. For children, it's 20 books or 10 hours of reading over the summer. For teens and adults, it's 8 books or equivalent time. Audiobooks and e-books count, as do graphic novels and magazines for children. We want reading to feel like fun, not homework.

**Q: What if we're going away for part of the summer?**
A: No problem at all. You can log your reading from anywhere – our online portal works on any device. If you're somewhere without internet, just keep a paper record and we'll update it when you're back. Many families do their logging in bursts when they return.

**Q: Can I register my whole family at once?**
A: Yes. Just bring everyone's library cards (or join them at the same time) and we'll set up a family account. You'll each get your own reading log, but you can manage them all from one login.

**Q: Are there prizes for adults too?**
A: Absolutely. We have separate prize pools for each age group, and every person who completes the challenge receives a certificate and a small prize. See below for the full prize details.

**Q: I registered before the original deadline – do I need to do anything again?**
A: No. If you registered before 30 November, you're already in the system and you'll be included in the first prize draw. The extended deadline is only for new registrations.

**Prizes**

We're excited to confirm the full prize list for SRC 2025. Every participant who completes the challenge receives:

- A **SRC 2025 finisher certificate**
- A **library-branded bookmark and sticker pack**
- Entry into the **major prize draw**

Major prizes for the three age groups:

The major prize draw will take place on **Saturday 31 January 2026** at the Lakehaven Central Library. Winners will be notified by email and phone, and their names will be posted on our website (with permission) the following week.

**What Our 2024 Participants Thought**

We shared a couple of quotes in our earlier notice, but we've had so many lovely comments that we wanted to pass on a few more:

Your reading log will be available when you register – either as a printed booklet (collect it from any branch) or as a digital log on our website. The digital log is handy because you can update it from your phone and see your progress bars fill up. We've also added a new feature this year: you can set a personal goal for yourself, and we'll send you a little reminder (only if you opt in) if you haven't logged anything for a week.

## Summer Reading Challenge 2025 – Frequently Asked Questions (Updated 12 January)

We've had a fantastic response to the Summer Reading Challenge, and the team at Lakehaven City Libraries has put together a few answers to the questions we've been hearing most often at our branches and through our social media. If your question isn't covered here, please don't hesitate to ask at any service desk or email us at [summerreading@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au](mailto:summerreading@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au).

---

**1. I've lost my reading log booklet. Can I get a replacement?**

Yes! You can collect a new printed booklet from any Lakehaven City Libraries branch – just let staff know your name and the branch where you originally registered. Alternatively, you can switch to the digital log at any time. Your progress will be saved on our system either way, and we can help you transfer any entries you've already recorded. There's no charge for a replacement booklet, and you don't need to bring your original – we trust you!

---

**2. Do audiobooks and ebooks really count?**

They absolutely do. As Daniel mentioned in our earlier notice, audiobooks are a great option if you're short on time or prefer listening while you're on the go. Ebooks and e-audiobooks borrowed through our Libby and BorrowBox apps also count. The only thing we ask is that you log each item separately – so if you listen to an audiobook that is also available in print, you can only count it once. We're happy to help you set up the apps if you're not sure how to use them.

---

**3. My child is 12 and turning 13 during the challenge. Which age group do they go in?**

We base the age group on the age the participant is at the time of registration. So if your child is 12 when they register, they'll be in the Children (0–12) category for the whole challenge, even if they turn 13 in January. This keeps things simple and ensures everyone has a fair chance. If you have any questions about which category applies, just ask at your branch.

---

**4. Can I register my whole family at once?**

You can, but each family member needs their own reading log and their own registration. This is because we need to track individual progress and, of course, each person needs to be in the draw for their own prizes. You can register everyone at the same time at a branch, or you can do it online by filling in the form for each person. It only takes a couple of minutes.

---

**5. What happens if I finish my 8 books before the challenge ends?**

Keep going! There's no limit to how many items you can log, and while the major prize draw is based on completing the challenge, the weekly random draws are open to anyone who has logged at least one item that week. So if you finish early, you can keep logging and you'll still be in the running for the smaller prizes. Plus, you'll have bragging rights at your book club.

---

**6. I'm a teacher. Can I sign up my class?**

We love this question! While the Summer Reading Challenge is designed for individuals and families, we do have a separate school programme that runs during term time. For the summer challenge, teachers are very welcome to join as individuals, but we can't register a whole class under one log. If you'd like to know more about our school programmes, please contact our Children's and Youth Services team at [kids@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au](mailto:kids@lakehaven.nsw.gov.au).

---

**7. Is there a cost to participate?**

No, the Summer Reading Challenge is completely free. All you need is a library membership, which is also free for anyone who lives, works, or studies in the Lakehaven City Council area. If you're not already a member, you can join online or at any branch in about five minutes. You'll need to bring some identification with your current address – a driver's licence, a rates notice, or a utility bill are all fine.

---

**8. I registered online but haven't received my confirmation email. What should I do?**

First, check your spam or junk folder – sometimes emails from our system get filtered out. If it's not there, please call us on 02 5550 3400 during opening hours and we'll check that your registration went through. You can also email us and we'll respond within two business days. Please note that the confirmation email contains your reading log link, so it's worth getting that sorted early.

**FINAL REMINDER – SUMMER READING CHALLENGE 2025**

**Registrations close this Friday, 12 December, at 5:00 pm.**

If you haven't signed up yet, now is the time. The challenge officially starts on Monday, 15 December, and runs through to Sunday, 1 February 2026. That's eight weeks of reading, logging, and prize draws – and it's all free.

We know life gets busy, so here's a quick rundown of everything you need to do before the deadline. Don't leave it to Friday afternoon – the online form has been known to slow down when everyone remembers at once.

---

**1. The deadline in one line**

Registrations close **5:00 pm, Friday 12 December 2025**. No late entries, no exceptions – the system simply won't accept new registrations after that time. If you're reading this on Friday, please don't wait until 4:55.

---

**2. What you need to register**

You'll need:

- A library membership (free if you live, work, or study in the Lakehaven City Council area – see question 7 below if you're not sure)
- An email address you check regularly (your reading log link is sent there)
- A few minutes – the form takes about two minutes per person

That's it. No proof of reading is required at registration. You only start logging books once the challenge begins.

---

**3. How to register – step by step**

1. Go to the library website: **lakehaven.nsw.gov.au/library**
2. Click the big green "Summer Reading Challenge" banner on the homepage
3. Select "Register now" – you'll be taken to the online form
4. Fill in your details. If you're registering children under 16, you'll need a parent or guardian's consent and email address
5. Submit the form – you'll see a confirmation screen straight away
6. Check your email for the confirmation message containing your personal reading log link

**Important:** If you register more than one person (for example, yourself and your two kids), you'll receive a separate confirmation email and reading log link for each person. Keep them somewhere safe – you'll use them all summer.

---

**4. Last-minute questions – quick answers**

**Q: I registered last week but never got my confirmation email. What should I do?**

First, check your spam or junk folder – sometimes emails from our system get filtered out. If it's not there, please call us on 02 5550 3400 during opening hours and we'll check that your registration went through. You can also email us and we'll respond within two business days. Please note that the confirmation email contains your reading log link, so it's worth getting that sorted early.

**Q: Can I register in person at a branch?**

Yes. All five branches (Lakehaven Central, Eastside, Northgate, Riverside, and the Harbour Street Pop-Up) have staff who can help you complete the form. You'll need to come in before closing time on Friday – branch hours vary, so check the website. The Pop-Up closes at 4:00 pm on Fridays, so that one's earlier than the others.

**Q: I've changed my email address since I registered. Can I update it?**

Yes – call us on 02 5550 3400 and we can update your contact details. Please do this **before** the challenge starts, because once the reading log link is sent out, it's tied to the original email. If you've already received your link and your email changes, you'll need to let us know so we can resend it.

**Q: Do I need to bring anything if I register in person?**

Just your library card or some identification if you're not a member yet. Staff can look up your membership with your name and address if you've forgotten your card.

**Q: My child wants to do the challenge but they're 4 years old. Is that okay?**

Absolutely. The challenge is open to all ages – babies, preschoolers, school kids, teens, and adults. For pre-readers, parents or carers can log books that are read aloud to them. It all counts.

**Q: What if I'm going away during the summer holidays?**

No problem. The reading log is online, so you can log from anywhere with an internet connection. There's no requirement to visit a branch during the challenge period, though we'd love to see you at our storytime sessions and craft days if you're around.

**Local History Talks** – *continued from page 5*

**The History of Lakehaven’s Tram Network** – Lakehaven Central. Join local historian Dr. Margaret Chen for a illustrated talk on the rise and fall of the tram system that once connected our suburbs. Includes rarely seen photographs from the City Archives. Saturday 25 October, 2:00–3:30 pm. Bookings essential.

**Early Farming Families of the Westgate Plains** – Westgate. Presented by the Westgate & District Historical Society. A look at the pioneering families who settled the area in the 1860s and their legacy today. Saturday 1 November, 10:30 am–12:00 pm. Afternoon tea provided.

**Remembering the 1974 Flood** – Northpoint. A community oral history session. Bring your own memories, photographs, or objects to share. This is part of an ongoing project to build a digital archive of the flood. Saturday 8 November, 1:00–3:00 pm. All welcome, no bookings needed.

**Hidden Histories: Women in Lakehaven’s Past** – Eastwood. A talk and discussion exploring the often-unrecorded contributions of women to our city’s development. Saturday 15 November, 2:00–3:30 pm. Presented in partnership with Eastwood Historical Group.

---

**Children’s and Family Programs** – *see page 3 for full details*

**Rhyme Time** – All branches. A fun, free session of songs, rhymes, and finger plays for babies and toddlers aged 0–2. Sessions run during school terms only. See page 3 for branch times.

**Storytime** – All branches. Stories and craft for children aged 3–5. Sessions run during school terms only. See page 3 for branch times.

**Lego Club** – Lakehaven Central, Eastwood, and Westgate. Build, create, and problem-solve with our massive Lego collection. For ages 6–12. Fortnightly on Saturdays during school terms. Check the website for dates and times.

**Junior Book Club** – Northpoint. For ages 8–12. Read a different book each month and join the discussion. Meets on the last Thursday of the month, 4:00–5:00 pm. Copies of the book are available at the front desk. New members always welcome.

**Family History for Kids** – Lakehaven Central. A hands-on workshop for ages 8–12 and their carers. Learn how to use the library’s family history resources to discover your own family story. Saturday 22 November, 10:00–11:30 am. Bookings essential.

**School Holiday Programme** – *see dedicated brochure for full details*. The Spring school holiday programme runs from 27 September to 12 October. Pick up a copy at any branch or view it online. Highlights include Lego Club: Build a City, Teen Writers’ Workshop, Science Experiments: Slime and More, and Movie Afternoon. All school holiday activities are free, but bookings are essential for most sessions.

---

**Adult Programs and Book Clubs**

**Page Turners Book Club** – Lakehaven Central. Meets on the first Tuesday of the month, 6:30–8:00 pm. Current reading: *The Dictionary of Lost Words* by Pip Williams. New members welcome. Copies available at the front desk.

**Mystery Readers** – Eastwood. A book club for fans of crime and mystery fiction. Meets on the second Wednesday of the month, 2:00–3:30 pm. Contact the Eastwood branch for the current reading list.

**Afternoon Book Club** – Westgate. Meets on the third Thursday of the month, 1:30–3:00 pm. All genres welcome. New members welcome. Copies of the current book are available at the Westgate front desk.

**Page Turners Book Club** – Northpoint. Meets on the last Wednesday of the month, 6:30–8:00 pm. Currently reading *The Lost Flowers of Alice Hart* by Holly Ringland. New members always welcome.

**Non-Fiction Book Club** – Lakehaven Central. For readers who prefer true stories. Meets on the third Monday of the month, 6:00–7:30 pm. See the website for the current title.

**Creative Writing Group** – Eastwood. A supportive group for writers of all levels. Share your work, get feedback, and find inspiration. Meets on the second Saturday of the month, 10:30 am–12:30 pm. No bookings required.

**Mahjong Club** – Westgate. Come and play this classic tile-based game. All skill levels welcome. Meets on Monday afternoons, 1:00–4:00 pm. No bookings required.
